literal: King Cheng of Zhou and Emperor Zhao of Han were likewise not easy to encounter.
idiomatic: Even the Zhou of King Cheng or the Han of Emperor Zhao was scarcely met with again.

literal: Textual collation notes
idiomatic: Collation notes

literal: "But you take me as kin": in various editions the two characters "yi wo qin" (take me as kin) appear as the two characters "yi wo" (also me).
idiomatic: "But you take me as kin": editions read yi wo qin (take me as kin) as the two characters yi wo (also me).

literal: Cefu yuangu juan 286, Song edition as quoted above; Ming edition
idiomatic: Cefu juan 286, Song edition as above; Ming edition

literal: 〈page 3365〉
idiomatic: folio 3365

literal: reads the two characters "yi qin" (as kin).
idiomatic: has "yi qin" (as kin).

literal: Commentary: The phrase "but you also me" is unintelligible and clearly erroneous; now emended and supplied according to the Song edition of Cefu.
idiomatic: Note: "but you also me" makes no sense and is clearly corrupt; the text is emended per the Song Cefu.

literal: "Compared to the phoenix not yet arriving": in various editions "zhi" (arrive) is written as "yi" (one), with the note below "suspected"; now according to Cefu juan 269
idiomatic: "Compared to the phoenix not yet arriving": editions read zhi (arrive) as yi (one), with yi (suspect) in the note below; emended per Cefu juan 269

literal: 〈page 3184〉
idiomatic: folio 3184

literal: Corrected.
idiomatic: Emended.

literal: "Appointed his maternal uncle Pan Senggu as Administrator of Leling in Ji Province": in Beishi juan 19, Biography of Prince of Pengcheng Xie, "Leling" is written as "Changle."
idiomatic: "Appointed his maternal uncle Pan Senggu Administrator of Leling, Ji Province": Beishi juan 19 (Pengcheng Wang Xie) reads Leling as Changle.

literal: Commentary: Ji Province has Changle but not Leling; Leling belongs to Qing Province—see juan 106, Monograph on Geography, upper and middle.
idiomatic: Note: Ji had Changle but not Leling; Leling was in Qing—Geography monograph juan 106, upper and middle.

literal: This biography ought to be erroneous.
idiomatic: The life is in error.

literal: "At that time the people of Qi Province, Liu Jun, Fang Qing, and others, stirred up the Three Qi; Xiao Yan sent generals Peng Qun, Wang Bian, and others to harass the frontier": in juan 9, Annals of Emperor Suzong, third month of the third year of Xiaochang, "Fang Qing" is written as "Fang Xu"; see collation note [20] to juan 9.
idiomatic: "At that time Qi people Liu Jun, Fang Qing, and others stirred the Three Qi; Xiao Yan sent Peng Qun, Wang Bian, and others to trouble the border": Suzong annals juan 9, Xiaochang year 3 month 3 reads Fang Qing as Fang Xu—see juan 9 collation note [20].

literal: Moreover in various editions below "Peng" there is the character "cheng" (city), and "qun" (cluster) is written as "jun" (commandery).
idiomatic: Editions also add cheng (city) after Peng and read qun (cluster) as jun (commandery).

literal: Commentary: juan 9, Annals of Emperor Suzong, first month of the third year of Xiaochang; juan 79, Biography of Lu Yu; Cefu juan 121
idiomatic: Note: Suzong annals juan 9, Xiaochang year 3 month 1; Lu Yu biography juan 79; Cefu juan 121

literal: 〈page 1451〉
idiomatic: folio 1451

literal: all read "Peng Qun, Wang Bian"; Peng Qun is a personal name.
idiomatic: all have "Peng Qun, Wang Bian"—Peng Qun is a man's name.

literal: Here "qun" (cluster) is corrupted as "jun" (commandery), and later people additionally inserted the character "cheng" (city) without basis.
idiomatic: Here qun (cluster) was miscopied as jun (commandery), and later scribes spuriously added cheng (city).

literal: Now according to this, deleted and corrected.
idiomatic: The text is now trimmed and emended accordingly.

literal: "Director of the Masters of Writing, minister": Commentary: above "xiang" (minister) the character "cheng" (director) has probably dropped, or below "xiang" the character "guo" (state) has dropped.
idiomatic: "Director of the Masters of Writing, minister": Note: cheng (director) may be missing before xiang (minister), or guo (state) after xiang.
